 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, challenging the award dated 19.12.2017 in MVC No.42/2016 passed by the I Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Addl.
MACT-IV, Chittradurga.

sentences.text: 2. The claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act, seeking just and proper compensation for injuries sustained in a road traffic accident on 03.07.2015.

The Tribunal attributed 20% contributory negligence to the claimant and awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,46,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the petition until actual realization.
This appeal is filed seeking enhancement of compensation.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company.
4. The Tribunal attributed 20% contributory negligence to the appellant/claimant, stating that the accident took place in the middle of the road.
However, the Tribunal has not provided reasons as to how the claimant contributed to the accident.

A perusal of the sketch at Ex.R1 indicated that the claimant joined the National Highway and, while he was in the middle of the road, the offending vehicle came from the wrong side and collided with the motorcycle.

The police, after investigation,
submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and not against the claimant.
In NC: 2024:KHC:22322 the absence of any evidence to establish that the claimant was negligent in riding the motorcycle, the negligence attributed to the claimant is not legally sustainable.
5. The appellant/claimant was aged 48 years on the date of the accident.
The claimant suffered fractures of both the tibia and fibula of the right leg in the road traffic accident and was an in- patient for 11 days.
6. The doctor, who was examined as PW.2, assessed the physical disability at 32.56%.
The functional disability assessed by the Tribunal at 10% is just and proper.
Given the nature of injuries, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is reassessed as follows:

In the result, the appeal is allowed-in-part.
The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.

The claimant is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.2,97,400/- as opposed to Rs.1,46,400/- awarded by the Tribunal.
8.
The enhanced compensation amount of Rs.1,51,000/- (i.e., 2,97,400-1,46,400) shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing the petition till the date of realization.

9. The respondent-Insurance Company is liable to pay entire compensation amount to the claimant and the same to be deposited with interest within a period of three months from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
10. The enhanced compensation with interest to be released in favour of the claimant.
To this extent, the impugned award stands modified.
